about: NVIDIA Xid knowledge base for DRSTool Crash Lab. Codes, mnemonics and NVIDIA's resolution buckets come from the NVIDIA Xid catalog (docs.nvidia.com/deploy/xid-errors). Triggers, workarounds and env links come from Linux reports on forums.developer.nvidia.com and are evidence, not proof: each one names its source. Weights are natural-log prior boosts (0 = no link, 1 ≈ ×2.7, 2 ≈ ×7.4) used by drstool_core.xid_analysis.

8.title: GPU stopped processing (watchdog)
8.summary: A channel stopped making progress and the driver watchdog killed it: a GPU hang, often reported as VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST by DXVK / vkd3d-proton.

evidence.note: Reproduced in several Vulkan games and by gpu-burn on the same machine: when a stress test alone triggers it, look at power, clocks and thermals before settings.
Reliable lockup under DXVK in one area of a game (Witcher 3): content-triggered hangs exist, so bisecting the configuration is still worth it when only one game does it.

remedies: If a GPU stress test also triggers it: remove overclocks / undervolts, check PSU cables and temperatures.

13.title: Graphics engine exception
13.summary: A shader or the graphics engine faulted. The detail after the code says how (illegal instruction, out-of-range address, MMU NACK). NVIDIA: if the same GPC/TPC repeats across runs it can be hardware; otherwise check the application.

subtypes.meaning: A shader instruction got an operand the hardware rejects — typically shader translation or a driver compiler path, frequently with ray tracing on.
The GPU decoded an instruction it does not know — a mis-compiled or corrupted shader binary (also seen with stale or corrupted shader caches).
A shader accessed memory outside its resource — descriptor / buffer bounds or robustness.
A shader access was refused by the MMU — an unmapped or freed page, close to Xid 31.
A command on the graphics channel raised an exception; read together with the other Xid 13 lines of the burst.

evidence.note: Metro Exodus Enhanced Edition / Control under vkd3d-proton with ray tracing: Xid 13 Illegal Instruction Parameter, also tied to resolution and settings; VKD3D_CONFIG=dxr,dxr11 was in use.
Metro Exodus EE on 515.43.04: Illegal Instruction Parameter bursts across many GPC/TPC — a driver/content issue, not a single bad SM.
Control with VKD3D_CONFIG=dxr,dxr11 freezing at one stage on 525.53.
Vulkan game with G-SYNC enabled crashed with Xid 13 when focus left the game (tab out).

remedies: Clear the game's shader caches (DXVK / vkd3d-proton / NVIDIA ~/.cache/nvidia) — a corrupted cache produces illegal-instruction faults.
If the very same GPC/TPC/SM repeats over several crashes and other games, run a GPU stress test: NVIDIA's workflow treats that as a possible hardware fault.

31.title: GPU memory page fault
31.summary: The GPU accessed an address with no valid mapping. FAULT_PDE means the whole page-directory entry is missing (often address 0 / garbage); FAULT_PTE means the page was unmapped or freed — use-after-free. NVIDIA: repeat it; faults on one GPU only may be hardware, otherwise check the application.

subtypes.meaning: Fault at address 0: a null GPU pointer — an uninitialised descriptor / buffer address.
No page-directory entry: the address was never mapped (wild pointer, out-of-bounds, stale descriptor).
No page-table entry: the page existed and is gone — resource freed while the GPU still used it.
The copy engine faulted: an upload / copy touched freed or unmapped memory.
Memory kind mismatch: an image / compression layout the access did not expect.

evidence.note: Monster Hunter Wilds with the descriptor heap path on 610 drivers: Xid 31 FAULT_PDE ACCESS_TYPE_VIRT_WRITE; downgrading to 595 helped.
Horizon Zero Dawn: Xid 31 FAULT_PDE at address 0 under Proton; the game ran with a 30 FPS cap and faulted above it.
Long-standing FAULT_PDE ACCESS_TYPE_READ reports in Proton games; a newer vkd3d-proton (2.9) circumvented it in one report — update the runner before bisecting.
UE 5.7 Vulkan, 5070 Ti, nvidia-open: removing gamescope only delayed the crash.

remedies: Update the runner (Proton / vkd3d-proton / DXVK): many Xid 31 reports were worked around on the translation-layer side.
If it began with a driver update, test the previous driver branch.

32.title: Invalid or corrupted push buffer stream
32.summary: The command stream the GPU fetched was malformed. In games it shows up as repeated pairs on one channel before a hang.

evidence.note: Hogwarts Legacy under vkd3d-proton: Xid 32 pairs on one channel, then a fatal Xid 56 and a DRM flip timeout ~20 min later; channel state had been left undefined by an earlier suspend/resume. Lowering the refresh rate to 144 Hz stopped it for the reporter.

remedies: Reboot instead of resuming from suspend before testing: a channel left broken by suspend keeps producing Xid 32.
Set NVreg_PreserveVideoMemoryAllocations=1 (with the nvidia suspend/resume hooks) if Xid 32 only appears after suspend.

43.title: GPU stopped processing (channel reset)
43.summary: The driver reset a channel that misbehaved; it follows the real error. Look at what came before it.

45.title: Preemptive cleanup after previous errors
45.nvidia: WORKFLOW_XID_45 · solo: restart, not solo: follow the other Xid
45.summary: Channels torn down because of an earlier error or because the process was killed. On its own after a game is closed it is harmless; next to other Xids it is a consequence, not the cause.

48.title: Double-bit ECC error
48.summary: Uncorrectable memory error (ECC-capable boards). A hardware event.

56.title: Display engine exception
56.summary: The display engine faulted. Usually followed by 'Flip event timeout' and a frozen desktop while the game itself is fine. Tied to refresh rate, VRR, multi-monitor and HDMI/DP links more than to game settings.

evidence.note: Xid 56 then a permanent flip timeout on KDE Wayland, dual DP 1440p@165 Hz, with no game running.
Multi-monitor freezes with Xid 56 on 575.64; disconnecting the HDMI cable stabilised it.
Flip event timeouts when VRR engages; disabling VRR was the temporary fix.
Lowering the refresh rate to 144 Hz stopped Xid 32 → Xid 56 hangs for one reporter.

remedies: Disable VRR / G-SYNC in the compositor and retest.
Lower the refresh rate or disconnect secondary displays to isolate a link problem.
This is a display-path fault: changing game env vars rarely helps; the search is unlikely to find a culprit.

61.title: Internal micro-controller breakpoint
61.summary: Firmware / power-management micro-controller event; a driver or firmware issue, not a game setting.

62.title: Internal micro-controller halt
62.summary: A GPU micro-controller halted. On recent drivers it opens the 62 → 45 → 119 → 154 cascade that needs a reboot.

evidence.note: RTX 5080, nvidia-open 590.48.01: Xid 62 → 45 → 119 (GSP timeout) → 154 desktop lockups across kernels.

remedies: Report with nvidia-bug-report.sh; try another driver branch. Env vars do not reach this layer.

68.title: NVDEC0 exception
68.summary: The video decoder faulted: in games, cutscene / video playback through NVDEC.

69.title: Graphics engine class error
69.summary: The GPU rejected a command recorded by the game / translation layer (Class Error with an ErrorCode). In Proton games it is most often a descriptor / binding path the driver mishandles.

evidence.note: vkd3d-proton's VK_EXT_descriptor_buffer path triggers Xid 69 on Pascal since the 535 drivers; bisected to the commit enabling global descriptor buffers; masking the extension works around it.
The Last of Us Part II on a 1080 Ti (575.64): Xid 69 Class c197, ErrorCode 4 within 20 s of gameplay.
Cyberpunk 2077 on a 1070 Ti: Xid 69; did not reproduce in a VM, so a driver path rather than hardware.

remedies: On Pascal: hide VK_EXT_descriptor_buffer from vkd3d-proton (VKD3D_DISABLE_EXTENSIONS=VK_EXT_descriptor_buffer) or use an older vkd3d-proton that predates it.

79.title: GPU has fallen off the bus
79.summary: The GPU stopped answering on PCIe. Causes are below the game: PCIe power management (ASPM), link errors, power delivery, firmware. Needs a reboot.

evidence.note: Xid 79 while idling when ASPM L0s is enabled in UEFI; disabling it there fixed it.
Lutris/Wine game: PCIe errors from an NVMe on the same bus preceded the GPU dropping off.
RTX 5070 Ti, 580.159.03 open: Xid 119 → 154 → SEC_FAULT → 79 cascade; DPM=0, persistence and pcie_aspm=off did not prevent it.

remedies: Disable PCIe ASPM in UEFI (kernel pcie_aspm=off is not always enough).
Look for AER / 'PCIe Bus Error' lines before it (other devices on the bus count).
Check power cables / PSU, reseat the card, update the BIOS.
Env vars cannot cause or prevent this; do not spend tests on the setting search.

109.title: Context switch timeout
109.summary: The GPU could not switch away from a context in time — a workload that will not yield (long dispatch, hang, deadlock between queues). Frequently a driver regression for specific games; content- and settings-dependent.

evidence.note: Starfield / Metro / Warframe / RE8 under vkd3d-proton: Xid 109 CTX SWITCH TIMEOUT; vkd3d-proton 2.10 worked around it for some; NVIDIA posted a Vulkan beta with a fix. Starfield was linked to view-map pressure.
595 drivers: the vkd3d-proton descriptor-heap path prevented the Xid 109 lockups for most games mentioned — turning it ON is a workaround there.
615 drivers: Xid 109 in a vkd3d-proton game with Reflex + Boost and heavy VRAM load.
Zone- and setting-dependent: disabling 'compute effects' (WoW) or lowering one visual-effects setting (UE5) stopped it — in-game settings matter as much as env vars.
Regression in 575 drivers (World of Warcraft) and in 595.45 (590.44.01 fine).
Crimson Desert on RTX 5090 / 595.58.03: VKD3D_CONFIG=no_upload_hvv,nodxr,single_queue did not help — a driver issue no flag fixes.

remedies: Try the previous / next driver branch: most Xid 109 waves were driver regressions.
Lower the in-game setting that drives heavy compute (effects, RT) to confirm a content trigger.
If it escalates to Xid 119/120/154 the GPU needs a reboot before the next test.

110.title: Security fault
110.summary: GPU security engine fault; seen inside GSP-timeout cascades before Xid 79.

119.title: GSP RPC timeout
119.summary: The driver's call into the GPU System Processor firmware timed out. The GPU is wedged until reset / reboot; often the end of a 109 or 62 cascade.

evidence.note: Xid 109 escalating to a GSP crash (119/120); NVreg_EnableGpuFirmware=0 used as a workaround (only on GPUs where GSP is optional — not Blackwell).
62 → 45 → 119 → 154 cascades on RTX 5080, nvidia-open 590.48.01.

remedies: Reboot before testing again: results after a GSP timeout are not meaningful.
Pre-Blackwell GPUs on the proprietary module: NVreg_EnableGpuFirmware=0 removes GSP from the path (the open module and Blackwell require GSP).
Report with nvidia-bug-report.sh; try another driver branch.

120.title: GSP error
120.summary: The GSP firmware itself faulted or panicked. Driver / firmware level.

evidence.note: Driver 580 GSP firmware crash (Xid 120/154) on an RTX 3070 Mobile with HDMI; 535 with GSP disabled worked.

remedies: Reboot; try another driver branch; on pre-Blackwell proprietary modules NVreg_EnableGpuFirmware=0.

154.title: GPU recovery action changed
154.summary: Informational: the driver says what recovery is now required (GPU reset, node reboot). It follows the real error.

167.title: PCIe fatal timeout
167.summary: PCIe transaction timed out; treat like Xid 79.

175.title: GSP RPC timeout (variant)
175.summary: Seen in forum reports right after Xid 119 as a GSP RPC timeout on GSP_RM_ALLOC; treat as part of the GSP cascade.

evidence.note: 595.71.05 open module: Xid 119/154/175 GSP collapse on a Dell G16 (RTX 3070 Ti Laptop).

cascades.title: Context-switch timeout escalated into a GSP firmware timeout
Micro-controller halt → GSP timeout → reset required
GSP timeout ended with the GPU dropping off the bus
Corrupted push buffers followed by a display-engine fault
